It has been suggested that, in addition to their hypoglycaemic effect, thiazolidinediones may have beneficial effects in the prevention of macrovascular diabetic complications, and there is some evidence that pioglita- zone may improve some cardiovascular outcomes (see Diabetic Complications, p.457). However, a meta-analysis1 of 42 studies found that, compared with either placebo or other antidiabetic drugs, rosiglitazone was associated with a significant increase in the risk of myocardial infarction, and an increase of borderline significance in death from cardiovascular causes.
